title: Schema-driven log multiplexer with trace-link tokens and tenant shard routing
creator: Lina Patel
description: Problem: Customers send heterogeneous structured logs (JSON + key=value) from SDKs, services, and third-party integrations. We need a scalable ingestion component that normalizes variants, attaches a single trace-link token (for joining logs/traces/metrics), and routes messages to the right downstream (Loki, ELK, long-term cold store) based on tenant, rate class, and schema. Scope: - Build a schema-driven multiplexer service (log-mux) that validates incoming payloads against a lightweight schema registry, extracts or generates a trace-link token (trace_link), enriches with tenant and service metadata, and routes to one or more outputs. - Provide dynamic routing rules: tenant-based shard, priority lanes (realtime vs batch), and fallbacks (ELK if Loki index is rate-limited). - Add admission control: per-tenant rate shaping, backpressure signals to producers (429 + Retry-After /x-retry headers), and a dead-letter path for schema failures. - Ensure trace linkage across spans and logs by propagating a stable trace_link token into log fields and into span attributes when available. Why different from earlier work: existing tickets focused on schema enforcement or correlation propagation separately; this ticket consolidates validation, token canonicalization, tenant sharding, and multiplex routing into a single adaptable service so downstream can rely on consistent trace linkage and routing semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Log-mux service deployed to staging and can validate at least three schema flavors (json-schema v7, simple key=value, and nested arrays).
Incoming log with X-Trace-Link header results in preserved trace_link field in downstream Loki and ELK documents.
If no trace header, service generates a stable trace_link (UUIDv7 or monotonic prefix) and includes it in all routed outputs and emitted spans.
Tenant routing rules can be updated via config and take effect without service restart (hot-reload).
Backpressure behavior observed under synthetic load: producers receive 429s with Retry-After when tenant queue > 90% capacity and Loki sink is saturated.
Schema failures are sent to dead-letter S3 bucket with a rejection reason header and retained for 30 days.
End-to-end test demonstrates joining a trace (OpenTelemetry) with three log lines using trace_link; dashboard shows correct latency and error counts.
design_decisions: Schema registry: lightweight HTTP + gRPC endpoint storing canonical json-schema v7 + simple pattern rules. Avoid heavy Avro ecosystem to keep ingestion fast.

Trace-link format: UUIDv7 with an embedded epoch to support ordering and reasonable cardinality; compatible with existing trace IDs but stored in a dedicated 'trace_link' field to avoid breaking downstream indexes.
Routing engine: rule-based virtual table evaluated in-memory, with changefeed from a central config store (Consul/etcd) for hot updates.
Sinks: primary is Loki (structured labels + JSON payload), fallback is ELK indexing (if Loki rejects or is rate-limited), and archival writes to S3 for non-realtime data.
Backpressure: implement token-bucket per-tenant plus global circuit-breaker; communicate via HTTP 429 and a small JSON body describing next-step (retry, drop, escalate).
implementation_tasks: proto: define ingestion API and trace_link header semantics (spec in repo: observability/log-mux/spec.md).
schema-registry: implement CRUD and validation endpoints + unit tests.
ingest worker: parse payloads, normalize variants, validate against schema, enrich metadata, generate/preserve trace_link.
routing: evaluate and apply routing rules, fanout to selected sinks with at-least-once semantics and dedup keys.
backpressure & quotas: per-tenant token-bucket, circuit breaker, and Retry-After header implementation.
dead-letter: store schema/validation rejects to S3 with retention lifecycle and index for searchability.
integration tests: end-to-end tests exercising Loki/ELK fallback, backpressure, and trace joining.
docs + SDK updates: update Node/Python SDKs to include automatic trace_link header propagation when available.
dashboards: create Grafana panels for ingestion latency, queue occupancy, per-tenant error rates, and trace_link join success rate.
rollout_plan: Stage: deploy to internal staging cluster with 10 synthetic tenants and run stress harness for 48 hours.
Canary: enable for 5 real tenants under feature flag (10% traffic) for 1 week; monitor CPU, latencies, error rates.
Gradual Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks if no regressions.
Fallback: if Loki saturates or error rate > 2% sustained, automatically route new writes to ELK and alert on-call.
Post-mortem: collect metrics and hold a retro after full ramp to capture tuning parameters and next steps.
monitoring_and_metrics: trace_link.join_success_ratio (percentage of traces with >=1 joined log within 60s)
blockers: Finalizing trace_link format canonicalization with OpenTelemetry team (waiting on OTEL-257 alignment).
Loki ingestion throttling semantics not fully documented; need ops confirmation for retry behavior.
